episode_title: ...Community is an output, not an input

real_qa.q: What is the core marketing challenge of selling kids beverages when the decision-maker is the parent, not the child?
real_qa.r: Products made for kids have to win twice: first with the kid to build desirability through packaging and taste, then with the parent by making it easy to say yes through clean nutrition and positioning it as an everyday treat rather than a big indulgence. No Biggie tested plain aluminum cans with 500 families to validate taste without visual bias, then designed the full experience with game boards and prompts to appeal to both audiences simultaneously.
real_qa.requete: how to market kids products to parents

real_qa.q: What do brands fundamentally misunderstand about building community as a growth strategy?
real_qa.r: Community is an output, not an input. Brands cannot force community by simply creating affiliate programs or branded WhatsApp groups. True community emerges only when you authentically create connection and people relate to one another on shared values and shared experiences, not through algorithms or mass emails.
real_qa.requete: community is output not input marketing

guest.bio_context: Allie Weiss started her career at BlackRock in corporate strategy, where she worked on the iShares ETF business for five years. She then joined Harry's, the razor company, in 2014 as part of the early D2C wave, before spending seven years at Glossier as CMO, scaling the beauty brand from its earliest days. She subsequently worked at a venture studio focused on zero-to-one building for family-focused consumer companies before launching No Biggie in May.

real_quote: Community is an output and not an input. The biggest mistake you can make is thinking that community is an input.
